title: “Because Of” Audit
opening: List the conditions you connect to mattering. Then inspect what each one does and what remains if it changes.

labels.example: Change the project result while keeping the same person in view. Then inspect the proposition below; the illustration does not answer it for you.

outcomeCaptions.ready: This model shows the project ready to ship. The person figure stays the same.
outcomeCaptions.repair: This model shows a displaced project panel that needs repair. The person figure stays the same.

labels.proposition: “If this launch fails, I have no right to exist.”
labels.propositionQuestion: Does the changed project outcome establish this proposition? You may leave the question open.
labels.empty: No reasons listed. Add one whenever you are ready.
labels.columnRemains: What remains when this condition is removed?
labels.kindLabel: How does it seem to fit?
labels.kindHelp: Conditional depends on an action or outcome; intrinsic rests on existence.
labels.remainsLabel: What remains if it changes or disappears?
labels.noticeHeading: Notice before trying to change it
labels.notice: Which conditions feel essential? How do they shape your feelings or decisions? You may leave any answer uncertain.

source.distinctions: The three source columns and five actions are preserved. Conditions are observations to inspect, not a diagnosis. A project may need repair or accountability; its result does not establish that a person lacks a right to exist.
source.limits: The example is instructional material, not a learner result. The audit does not force a positive feeling, a conclusion, or a changed condition. Local Classroom evidence does not establish effectiveness, author acceptance or live canonical readback.
